question: Can a lexically explicit relation sigil separate open semantic relation identity from identifiers/operators while preserving compact G9 source and supporting arbitrary relation identities through a quoted fallback?

source_basis.prior_counterevidence: E2B replication exposed relation-word lexical ambiguity under the first compatibility patch

candidate.resolver_rule: parsed relation identity must resolve against a declared typed relation symbol; parser acceptance alone is not semantic acceptance
candidate.authority_rule: relation resolution never grants execution authority

concurrent_comparison.interpretation: Both strict candidates survive local fuzz at tested scope. The sigil hybrid is materially more compact on the same comparison axis, while the generic quoted-call candidate has a simpler universally quoted canonical surface. Neither is selected before full-corpus/reader/diagnostic comparison.

interpretation.supports: A sigil-prefixed open-relation surface with quoted fallback can remove identifier-vs-relation lexical ambiguity, preserve arbitrary relation identity, and stay close to current G9 surface cost without semantic redesign.
interpretation.next_falsifier: Implement sigil-hybrid, strict generic quoted-call, and declared contextual bare-infix candidates in the real BASE parser; run complete admitted G9+dialect corpus, roundtrip semantic_hash, mutation/fuzz, diagnostics and actual reader/token/repair benchmarks.
